messages:
support_jake: FYI customer (acme-corp) opened an urgent ticket for their Private deployment. After the infra team applied a default-deny firewall profile they started seeing 403s from the Redwood API, big latency spikes, and no audit-log rows for a ~2h window. KMS decrypt errors in their app logs. Repro steps below.

customer_ops: +1, this started right after we rolled the new egress rules. Impacting production traffic. Billing also spiked (we saw a burst of retries).

support_jake: Repro steps I used (from a host in the customer's private subnet):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  https://private-api-us-west-2.redwood.local/v1/generate \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
# response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n# app log: "kms: Decrypt failed: AccessDenied"\n```

maria_sen: :eyes: Do we have their VPC endpoint config? If they removed outbound to kms/s3 that would explain both KMS and audit delivery. Also retries = latency + billing hit.

jon_platt: I pulled the customer's firewall rules. They switched to default-deny and only allowed 443 to a small set of service IPs. They didn't add the regional KMS/VPC endpoint IPs or S3 endpoints. They also blocked outbound to telemetry.collector.redwood.com.

sre_anna: Can someone run a quick tcpdump to confirm TCP resets to kms endpoints? Suggest checking for 10.1.2.3:443 in their egress block (this is one of their NAT IPs for KMS traffic).

devops_lee: quick test run from a host in the same subnet shows TLS handshake to kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com failing with RST. I can reproduce the 403 by blocking egress to KMS.

maria_sen: Actionable remediation (short-term): add explicit egress allow to the customer's KMS endpoint(s) and to S3 (for audit log delivery), and allow telemetry endpoint. Long-term: add VPCE for kms and s3 or document required egress list in private deploy guide.

support_jake: Suggested firewall rules (customer asked for exact lines):
```
# security-group style (AWS)
Outbound: allow TCP 443 to kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com (or VPCE CIDR)
Outbound: allow TCP 443 to s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
Outbound: allow TCP 443 to telemetry.collector.redwood.com
# if using on-prem firewall, allow 443 to the same FQDNs or IP ranges
```

jon_platt: Note: if they use a customer-managed HSM (on-prem or cloud-hsm) we need ports for the HSM management protocol open too. Also confirm their HSM client has the right IAM role to call KMS (we're seeing AccessDenied in logs).

sre_anna: For audit-proofing: we found no audit rows between 2026-03-16T02:10 and 2026-03-16T04:30. Likely because logs couldn't reach S3. When you re-enable egress please check /var/log/redwood/audit-uploader.log on their collector for error lines like "s3: PutObject failed: AccessDenied or Timeout".

devops_lee: Temporary mitigation applied (with customer approval): added egress to KMS + S3 + telemetry for the affected subnets. Confirmed API responses recovered and latency normalized.

customer_ops: Customer validated: API OK, latency back to normal, billing spike reduced (they will follow up on the retry charge question). They asked for a postmortem and a checklist to avoid this in future.

maria_sen: Postmortem owners: @jon_platt to follow up with customer infra on VPCE or NAT config; @devops_lee to update the private-deploy docs with a required egress table; @sre_anna to add an alert that flags missing audit uploads for >15m.

jon_platt: I'll draft the postmortem and include a TTL-based check for missing audit rows + a runbook for rollback (how to re-open egress safely).

sec-bot: Incident assigned: ENG-SEC-2026-042, severity: S2, owner: jon_platt. Links: https://pm.redwood.local/incidents/ENG-SEC-2026-042

support_jake: Thanks all. If anyone finds IAM misconfig for their KMS role (why AccessDenied happened after egress added) please ping the thread.

maria_sen: Follow-up note: also verify customer isn't routing KMS traffic through a proxy that enforces a TLS SNI whitelist; that can silently break endpoints when FQDNs change.

sre_anna: Closing the loop: verified audit logs resumed and packets to S3 succeed. Leaving this open for the postmortem + docs updates. :white_check_mark:
